analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. It adds two documentation rows after line 558 in the base text, at head lines 559-561. They describe DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION, which are memory and buffer-cache reclaim controls. Both default on and are disabled only by exact `0`. The first is described as forwarded to the launchd job. No code changed in the supplied evidence, so no runtime control was weakened. I examined the three units: base lines 509-703, which hold the surrounding config tables, the SSD prefix cache section and the GPT-OSS controls, and head lines 1-353, which are documentation-only. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the second row was not visible. The head units supplied do not show the added lines at 559-561, because head_text covers only lines 1-353. The rows are therefore reviewed from the patch only.

Relevant threat IDs are T-028, residual KV data in GPU memory, and T-041, the prefix cache. The segment-retention row says KV segments are held "uncommitted and uncharged" and reinstalled at admission without allocating, filling or fencing new ones. If that is accurate, it could extend how long residual KV data stays in memory across requests and tenants. Segments are dropped on refused admission, memory pressure, before load gates and after 30 s idle. This is a behavior change that may touch T-028 residue and zeroing assumptions, but the documentation alone does not show whether retained segments are scrubbed or scoped per tenant. This is an integration question for the code-side review of EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift and KVPoolReclaimer.swift, not a finding here.

The SSD cache, encryption, TTL and attestation boundaries are untouched. No threat-model assumption is contradicted by the visible documentation. needs_deeper_review is true only for the unverified T-028 interaction in the underlying code changes.
